claims.claim: An alleged optimum has a linear-time verifiable certificate, even for arbitrary signed entries.
claims.evidence: In the unit-cost exact-arithmetic model, construct a two-dimensional prefix table in O(mn). For L>0, checking every L-square costs at most mn queries; for L=0 feasibility is vacuous. One valid violating square for each length l>L proves every larger length infeasible, and there are at most q=min(m,n)<=mn such witnesses. Conversely, an accepted certificate proves L feasible and every larger length infeasible, hence proves exact optimality without any monotonicity assumption.
claims.search_method: Proved soundness, completeness, and the operation bound directly; exhaustively checked acceptance iff L is optimal for 44,513 alleged certificates over 14,966 signed-matrix/threshold instances, including L=0.

claims.claim: There is an exact output-sensitive search algorithm whose worst-case time is O(mn min(m,n)).
claims.evidence: Descending exhaustive search returns the first feasible side, which is the maximum feasible side even when feasibility is nonmonotone. For m>=n=q and l=q-t, there are (m-n+t+1)(t+1) placements. Through d=q-L this sums exactly to (m-n+1)(d+1)(d+2)/2+d(d+1)(d+2)/3, yielding the stated output-dependent bound and O(mnq) when d<=q. If L=0, the algorithm tests only t=0,...,q-1; including t=q is a valid extra upper-bound term. Stored violations supply the claim-0 certificate.
claims.search_method: Derived the placement count and closed form exactly, then compared descending search with brute-force optima on 14,966 signed instances and checked 38,251 performed placement tests against the bound.

claims.claim: Feasibility can alternate at every side length, and the natural no-revisit greedy extension is incorrect.
claims.evidence: In the stated family, an even-length interval of the alternating first row sums to zero, while an odd-length interval sums to either 1 or -1; squares below that row sum to zero. Thus F_l=0 for even l and F_l=1 for odd l, so feasibility at k=0 flips at every consecutive length. In the 2-by-3 example, the side-2 sums are 1 and 4. After the second fails, continuing at side 1 without revisiting earlier positions encounters only 1,-3,1,1, yet the skipped entry 2 violates k=1. Both side lengths are infeasible, so the correct L=0 answer is 0 rather than 1.
claims.witness: Alternation: first row (1,-1,1,-1,...) with all other rows zero and k=0. Greedy failure: [[2,1,1],[-3,1,1]] with k=1.
claims.search_method: Proved the interval-sum identities and reproduced every F_l for all dimensions 1 through 64, totaling 2,080 checked side lengths; separately executed the stated no-revisit trace exactly.

claims.claim: The O(mn) endpoint is achievable for two nontrivial signed separable classes: multiplicative rank one and additive separability.
claims.evidence: For A_ij=u_i v_j, an l-square sum is xy for independent row- and column-window sums. Its maximum over the enclosing rectangle of possible x,y values occurs among the four products of their extrema. With a matrix pivot p, the corresponding values are four exact numerators divided individually by p; taking the maximum after division handles p<0 correctly. The pivot identity is necessary and sufficient for rank at most one. For A_ij=u_i+v_j, the maximum is l(max X_l+max Y_l), and the displayed recognition identity is necessary and sufficient. Scanning one-dimensional windows for all q lengths costs O(q(m+n))<=O(mn), while recognition costs O(mn).
claims.search_method: Compared both formulas with brute-force square maxima for 23,775 signed rank-one and 1,467 signed additive factorizations; tested 11,456 negative first pivots and both recognition predicates on 21,766 arbitrary matrices using independent minor identities.

claims.claim: A thresholded max-plus-convolution scan embeds exactly into matrices supported on one row.
claims.evidence: For side B-t and horizontal start s, the first-row window telescopes to p_{B-(t-s)}-p_s. If s=i<N and j=t-i<N, this equals C+x_i+y_j and is at least 1. Every invalid start has either s>=N, giving at most C+W-H=-1, or j>=N, giving at most W-H<0. Squares starting below the supported row sum to zero, so the positive valid windows determine F_{B-t}=C+c_t. The three arbitrary middle prefix values are never endpoints for these windows. Therefore threshold C+K makes exactly those high side lengths with c_t<=K feasible, proving the stated answer mapping.
claims.witness: For N=2, x=(1,-2), y=(3,0), the construction with middle prefixes zero has B=8, C=7 and first row (3,9,-11,0,0,-11,18,3); its F_8,F_7,F_6 values are 11,8,5, equal to C+(4,1,-2).
claims.search_method: Reconstructed 22,146 one-row matrices using three unequal middle-prefix assignments, including 100-bit inputs; checked 149,508 coefficient identities, all 585,543 relevant valid/invalid windows, and 116,334 threshold-answer cases with integers only.

claims.claim: If integer bit lengths are unbounded and bit operations are charged, an O(mn) bound independent of bit length is impossible.
claims.evidence: On an explicit-binary bit-cost model, the 1-by-1 instance requires deciding whether a<=k. At a=k=2^(B-1), if a deterministic exact algorithm leaves any lower bit r unexamined, the same observations arise for a'=k+2^r although the correct feasibility answer changes. Hence the equality execution must inspect B-1 lower bits and costs Omega(B), contradicting a bit-time bound O(mn)=O(1) independent of B. This model-specific input-length lower bound does not exclude O(mn) word operations.
claims.witness: For every B>=2 and 0<=r<B-1, compare (a,k)=(2^(B-1),2^(B-1)) with (a',k)=(2^(B-1)+2^r,2^(B-1)); the encodings have equal length and differ in exactly one lower bit, while the 1-square changes from feasible to infeasible.
claims.search_method: Proved the indistinguishability lower bound and checked all 32,640 single-bit alternatives for B=2,...,256 exactly.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a general O(mn) algorithm for signed integer matrices at the intended bounded-word/unit-cost strength or a matching impossibility result under a standard assumption. The draft explicitly proves neither and says so in its opening and closing paragraphs. Its verifier, O(mn min(m,n)) search, alternating obstruction, two separable subclasses, and one-row embedding are correct material progress. The unbounded-bit Omega(B) observation is only a generic input-encoding obstruction and does not resolve the substantive word-RAM endpoint. Accordingly, PARTIAL is accurate and the final writeup does not overclaim target coverage.
